Ratio of female to male labor force part.descriptionShort: This ratio is calculated by dividing the labor force participation rate among women by the corresponding rate for men. The labor force participation rate is the share of the working-age population (ages 15 and over) who are economically active (employed or unemployed).
Ratio of female to male labor force part.descriptionKey:
- This data comes from the Modelled Estimates series of the International Labour Organization (ILO). The series mixes two kinds of values. Where a country reported data for a year, the ILO adjusts it to common international definitions. Where it did not, the ILO fills the gap with an estimate from a statistical model, so that it can calculate regional and global figures for every year. These model estimates are highly uncertain, especially for countries with little reported data: the World Bank advises against using them to compare or rank countries, and the ILO says to use them with great care. You can read more about how the ILO produces these estimates in the [Modelled Estimates documentation](https://ilostat.ilo.org/methods/concepts-and-definitions/ilo-modelled-estimates/).
- This data follows the standards of the 13th International Conference of Labour Statisticians (ICLS). Under this framework, employment includes work for pay or profit, including self-employment, as well as the production of goods for own use (such as subsistence farming). Changes in the definition of employment also affect who is counted as unemployed or outside the labor force. Because definitions were updated under the 19th ICLS, data using the newer definitions is not fully comparable with data based on the 13th ICLS. You can read more about the definitions in [this explainer by the ILO](https://www.ilo.org/publications/quick-guide-understanding-impact-new-statistical-standards-ilostat).
